check: Grain: one row per store, product and date
decision_impact: Duplicate days would double-count demand and stockout hours

check: Complete panel: every series has 90 train + 7 eval consecutive days
decision_impact: Missing days would read as zero demand in the 28-day features

check: Hourly sales sum to daily sales
decision_impact: Hourly recovery would not reconcile with reported daily sales

check: stock_hour6_22_cnt equals the hourly flags for hours 6 to 21
decision_impact: Confirms the publisher's selling window is 06:00 to 21:59 (16 hours), not 06:00 to 22:59
treatment: Selling window fixed at hours 6 to 21 in config/params.json

check: Hierarchy: each product in one category path, each store in one city
decision_impact: Category and city roll-ups would split or double-count

check: Sales recorded in an out-of-stock hour that follows another out-of-stock hour
decision_impact: 353,530 days have sales in some flagged hour; most are the sell-out hour itself (sold out mid-hour). The stricter rule leaves 248,080 days (1.0% of window sales) where the flag and the till disagree, so a flag is evidence of a stockout, not proof
treatment: Recorded sales are kept and recovered demand is floored at them; series with 3+ such days get a 'check the stock-status feed' item on the review list

check: Out-of-stock flags outside the selling window (22:00 to 05:59)
decision_impact: Counting all 24 hours puts 24.7% of hours and 59.8% of days out of stock; the selling window gives 19.7% of hours and 44.0% of days. 93% of 00:00 flags follow a stockout at 21:00 the evening before, so a 24-hour KPI counts one evening sell-out on two days
treatment: Every availability KPI uses the selling window only

check: Out of stock for the whole selling window
decision_impact: No in-stock hour to recover from (35,937 of these days still record sales). Imputing a typical day would add 21% to estimated lost demand, an assumption the masking test cannot check (a whole-day stockout may also be a ranging decision)
treatment: Reported as 'unavailable days', kept out of the lost-demand target and the scores

decision_impact: discount = 0 (published meaning: free) on these rows comes with sales 16x the average: more likely a missing-value code than a giveaway. Discount is not used by any score
treatment: Flagged only; would need publisher confirmation before any price-effect analysis
